name: nebu

secrets:
  internal_secret:
    file: .secrets/internal_secret
  minio_root_user:
    file: .secrets/minio_root_user
  minio_root_password:
    file: .secrets/minio_root_password
  # Story 12.3 — IAM credentials for the nebu-app MinIO user (least-privilege: PutObject+GetObject only).
  # Generated by `make setup`. Used by the media gateway and the createbuckets init container.
  minio_app_access_key:
    file: .secrets/minio_app_access_key
  minio_app_secret_key:
    file: .secrets/minio_app_secret_key

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: nebu
      POSTGRES_USER: nebu
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-nebu_dev_password}
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U nebu -d nebu"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      # Story 5.29a — AC2: DB-init script provisions nebu_migrate and nebu_app roles
      # on first container start (docker-entrypoint-initdb.d runs only on empty volumes).
      - ./dev/postgres/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro

  # go-removal-cleanup (full-elixir-stack): the Go `gateway:` service was removed.
  # The Elixir `server:` service below now serves ALL public endpoints (Matrix CS API,
  # /_matrix/media, and the Phoenix LiveView admin /admin) on its single Bandit
  # listener (server:4000), published to the host on 8008 (Matrix) and 8080 (admin).
  # The server also owns the OIDC Authorization-Code + PKCE login flow and runs DB
  # migrations on startup (see server/Dockerfile + NEBU_DB_URL_MIGRATE below).
  server:
    build:
      context: ./server
      args:
        GIT_COMMIT: ${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}
        BUILD_TIME: ${BUILD_TIME:-unknown}
        RELEASE_VERSION: ${RELEASE_VERSION:-unknown}
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      # media-gateway-migration (AC6): the server now serves /_matrix/media/v3/* directly
      # (Elixir Nebu.Media), so it needs MinIO healthy and the bucket/IAM-user
      # created — exactly the dependencies the removed `media:` service had.
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy
      createbuckets:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    # media-gateway-migration (AC6): MinIO IAM credentials (file-based Docker
    # Secrets) consumed by Nebu.Media.Storage / config/runtime.exs ExAws config.
    secrets:
      - internal_secret
      - minio_app_access_key
      - minio_app_secret_key
    environment:
      # Story 5.29a — AC3: the server also uses nebu_app at runtime (no DDL from the server)
      NEBU_DB_URL: "postgresql://nebu_app:nebu_app_dev_pw@postgres:5432/nebu"
      DATABASE_URL: "ecto://nebu_app:nebu_app_dev_pw@postgres:5432/nebu"
      # go-removal-cleanup: migrations run as nebu_migrate (table owner) — ported from
      # the removed gateway service. server/Dockerfile invokes Nebu.Release.migrate/0 on
      # startup before the server boots, using this connection.
      NEBU_DB_URL_MIGRATE: "postgresql://nebu_migrate:nebu_migrate_dev_pw@postgres:5432/nebu"
      NEBU_INTERNAL_SECRET_FILE: "/run/secrets/internal_secret"
      NEBU_SERVER_NAME: "localhost"
      NEBU_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY: "${NEBU_PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY:-6465766b65793030303030303030303030303030303030303030303030303030}"
      # oidc-bootstrap-only-config (ADR-022): OIDC is configured EXCLUSIVELY through the
      # Bootstrap Wizard (server_config) — there are NO NEBU_OIDC_* / NEBU_ADMIN_OIDC_*
      # config variables. A single OIDC client (dev Dex `nebu-gateway`, secret
      # `nebu-dev-secret`, all redirect URIs registered in dev/dex/config.yaml) serves
      # both Matrix Bearer validation and admin operator login. On a fresh DB the server
      # boots fail-closed (all Bearer tokens 401, admin → /bootstrap); run the wizard
      # once (issuer http://dex:5556/dex, client nebu-gateway / nebu-dev-secret, audience
      # nebu-gateway, JWKS http://dex:5556/dex/keys) to configure it.
      #
      # NEBU_OIDC_JWKS_TTL is the JwksCache refresh interval (a cache-tuning knob, NOT
      # OIDC issuer/audience/client config) and may stay.
      NEBU_OIDC_JWKS_TTL: "300"
      # DEV-ONLY: this stack serves the admin UI over plain http://localhost, so the
      # admin session cookie must NOT be Secure (otherwise the login-state cookie is
      # not returned on the OIDC callback in stricter browsers → "Invalid login state").
      # Production serves over TLS and leaves this unset (defaults to secure:true).
      NEBU_ADMIN_SESSION_SECURE: "false"
      # Integration-test escape hatch: set NEBU_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED=true in the host
      # environment before `docker compose up` to disable the IP rate limiter.
      # make test-integration sets this automatically; never set in production.
      NEBU_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED: "${NEBU_RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED:-false}"
      # e2e-session-refresh-suites: Nebu session ceilings (default 8h, set in
      # Nebu.Web.SessionConfig). Leave empty for normal dev/prod (→ 8h). The
      # `make test-e2e-refresh` target sets these short on the host so the silent
      # OIDC-refresh loop fires within the test window. Empty / junk → 8h default
      # (parsed by SessionConfig.parse_ttl/1, never crashes the login path).
      NEBU_MATRIX_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS: "${NEBU_MATRIX_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS:-}"
      NEBU_ADMIN_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS: "${NEBU_ADMIN_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS:-}"
      # media-gateway-migration (AC6): media object storage, ported from the Go
      # `media:` service. Same MinIO bucket + nebu-app IAM credentials.
      NEBU_MINIO_ENDPOINT: "minio:9000"
      NEBU_MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_FILE: "/run/secrets/minio_app_access_key"
      NEBU_MINIO_SECRET_KEY_FILE: "/run/secrets/minio_app_secret_key"
      NEBU_MINIO_BUCKET: "nebu-media"
      NEBU_MINIO_USE_SSL: "false"
      # media-security-admin-control/3-clamav-genserver: ClamAV scanner client.
      # Nebu.Media.ClamAV tolerates clamd being unreachable at boot (AC7) — no
      # depends_on/healthy-gate is required here, clamd may come up after the
      # server (freshclam's first signature download can take a while).
      NEBU_CLAMAV_HOST: "clamav"
      NEBU_CLAMAV_PORT: "3310"
    ports:
      # go-removal-cleanup: the server now serves the public Matrix endpoint (host 8008)
      # and the admin UI (host 8080) — both formerly published by the Go gateway —
      # plus its own 4000. All three map to the single Bandit listener on server:4000.
      # (The gRPC network listener was removed — ADR-021; the server no longer opens port 9000.)
      - "8008:4000"
      - "8080:4000"
      - "4000:4000"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:4000/health"]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  dex:
    image: dexidp/dex:v2.45.1
    command: ["dex", "serve", "/etc/dex/config.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./dev/dex/config.yaml:/etc/dex/config.yaml:ro
      - dex_data:/var/dex
    ports:
      - "5556:5556"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -q -O- http://localhost:5556/dex/.well-known/openid-configuration || exit 1"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 5s

  element:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker/Dockerfile.element-e2e
    depends_on:
      # go-removal-cleanup: was gateway; the server now serves the public Matrix endpoint.
      server:
        condition: service_healthy
    ports:
      - "7070:80"
    profiles:
      - e2e

  # Story 12.1 — MinIO object storage (S3-compatible) for media uploads.
  # Credentials are read from Docker Secrets generated by `make setup` (.secrets/ is gitignored).
  # ADR-013: MinIO as S3-compatible object store for MVP.
  minio:
    image: minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: server /data --console-address ":9001"
    environment:
      # Story 12.1 — AC2: credentials read from Docker Secrets, not hardcoded.
      # WARNING: These are example credentials for local development only.
      # Replace before first production start.
      MINIO_ROOT_USER_FILE: /run/secrets/minio_root_user
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD_FILE: /run/secrets/minio_root_password
    ports:
      - "9000:9000"   # MinIO S3 API
      - "9001:9001"   # MinIO Console
    secrets:
      - minio_root_user
      - minio_root_password
    volumes:
      - minio_data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:9000/minio/health/live"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 10s

  # Story 12.1 — One-shot init container that creates the `nebu-media` bucket.
  # Story 12.3 — Extended: creates nebu-app IAM user with PutObject+GetObject policy only.
  # Runs after MinIO is healthy; exits 0 on success (idempotent — user/policy already exists is OK).
  createbuckets:
    # Story 12.7 — SEC Gate 2 fix [MEDIUM-4 + MEDIUM-6]:
    # - Bumped to 2026 release tag (security fix: Finding #6)
    # - Credentials passed via MC_HOST_minio env var and shell variables to keep secrets
    #   off argv (/proc/<pid>/cmdline) — defeats Docker Secrets goal if passed as mc args.
    #
    # 2026-07-30 correction: the `--stdin` form referenced above for `mc admin user add`
    # does not exist on this (or the current `latest`) mc release — verified via
    # `mc admin user add --help`, which only documents the positional
    # `TARGET ACCESSKEY SECRETKEY` form. The previous script silently swallowed the
    # resulting usage error via `|| true`, so the app IAM user was NEVER created —
    # every real S3 write from the server failed with an auth error (surfaced as
    # `{:error, {:put_failed, _}}` -> 500 "Failed to store media file"). Reverted to
    # the only syntax this tool actually supports; the secret values are therefore
    # briefly visible in this container's own argv for its few-second one-shot
    # lifetime (not persisted, not sent over the network in cleartext — MC_HOST_minio
    # still keeps the *root* credentials off argv). If a future mc release adds a real
    # stdin/file-based form for `admin user add`, switch back.
    #
    # Second bug found the same day: the policy-to-user attachment line called
    # `mc admin user policy attach ... --user X`, which doesn't exist either (`mc
    # admin user policy` is a read-only "export policy as JSON" command, and `--user`
    # isn't one of its flags) — its fallback, `mc admin policy set`, is itself a fully
    # removed/rejected command on this release, so BOTH attempts failed and the app
    # user never actually held the nebu-app-policy grants. The real command is the
    # top-level `mc admin policy attach TARGET POLICY --user USER`.
    image: minio/mc:RELEASE.2025-08-13T08-35-41Z
    depends_on:
      minio:
        condition: service_healthy
    secrets:
      - minio_root_user
      - minio_root_password
      - minio_app_access_key
      - minio_app_secret_key
    volumes:
      - ./dev/minio/nebu-app-policy.json:/policy/nebu-app-policy.json:ro
    entrypoint: |
      /bin/sh -c '
      export MC_HOST_minio="http://$(cat /run/secrets/minio_root_user):$(cat /run/secrets/minio_root_password)@minio:9000"
      mc mb --ignore-existing minio/nebu-media
      APP_KEY=$$(cat /run/secrets/minio_app_access_key)
      APP_SECRET=$$(cat /run/secrets/minio_app_secret_key)
      mc admin user add minio "$$APP_KEY" "$$APP_SECRET" || echo "createbuckets: user add failed or already exists (non-fatal)"
      mc admin policy create minio nebu-app-policy /policy/nebu-app-policy.json 2>/dev/null || mc admin policy add minio nebu-app-policy /policy/nebu-app-policy.json || true
      mc admin policy attach minio nebu-app-policy --user "$$APP_KEY" || echo "createbuckets: policy attach failed or already attached (non-fatal)"
      exit 0
      '

  # media-gateway-migration (AC6): the Go `media:` service was removed here. The
  # Elixir server now serves the deprecated /_matrix/media/v3/* endpoints directly
  # (Nebu.Media via the Bandit listener on server:4000), with the same MinIO
  # bucket + nebu-app IAM credentials now wired into the `server:` service above.
  # The minio + createbuckets services are intentionally retained.

  # media-security-admin-control/3-clamav-genserver — malware scanner daemon
  # (ADR-024: self-hosted ClamAV, no file content/hash leaves the deployment).
  # The official clamav/clamav image runs both clamd and freshclam (signature
  # updates) in one container by default — no separate sidecar needed for this
  # story's scope. Nebu.Media.ClamAV connects via NEBU_CLAMAV_HOST/PORT
  # (default "clamav"/3310, matching this service name on the default network).
  clamav:
    image: clamav/clamav:stable
    # No arm64 manifest is published for this image ("no matching manifest
    # for linux/arm64/v8"); pin amd64 explicitly so Docker Desktop's
    # Rosetta/QEMU emulation runs it on Apple Silicon dev hosts (same
    # emulated-pull pattern already implied by the dex service's platform
    # mismatch warning above), instead of a hard pull failure.
    platform: linux/amd64
    restart: unless-stopped
    # Kassandra security review (F-4, 2026-07-13): clamd has no
    # authentication and its control protocol includes verbs like SHUTDOWN
    # (a DoS on the scanner) — unlike postgres/minio, this is not a service
    # meant to be reachable from the host. `server` reaches it over the
    # compose network by service name (NEBU_CLAMAV_HOST=clamav), so no host
    # port publish is needed; deliberately no `ports:` mapping here.
    volumes:
      - clamav_data:/var/lib/clamav
    healthcheck:
      # Bundled in the clamav/clamav image specifically for container healthchecks.
      test: ["CMD", "clamdcheck.sh"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 5
      # freshclam's first signature database download can take a few minutes.
      start_period: 180s

volumes:
  postgres_data:
  dex_data:
  minio_data:
  clamav_data:

  Plain HTTP controller for the Bootstrap Wizard (device-management story,
  fix-bootstrap-wizard-liveview-bugs).

  Replaces the LiveView `Nebu.Admin.BootstrapLive` for the wizard steps 1-3.
  Fixes three bugs:

    1. Infinite redirect — the old live route was inside `live_session :admin` with

       there is no admin session, so the gate redirected to /admin/login, which
       redirected to /admin/bootstrap → infinite loop.

       (and thus form input values). Plain HTML POST forms + server-side redirects
       are not affected.

def callback(conn, params) do
    login_state = get_session(conn, @oidc_login_session_key)

    case validate_state(login_state, params["state"]) do
      :ok ->
        do_callback(conn, params, login_state)

      {:error, reason} ->
        Logger.warning("admin callback state rejected: #{inspect(reason)}")

        conn
        |> delete_session(@oidc_login_session_key)
        |> put_resp_content_type("text/plain")
        |> send_resp(400, "Invalid login state")
        |> halt()
    end
  end

  defp do_callback(conn, params, login_state) do
    conn = delete_session(conn, @oidc_login_session_key)
    mode = login_state["mode"]

    with {:ok, code} <- require_code(params),
         {:ok, cfg} <- oidc_config(mode),
         {:ok, claims, refresh_token} <- exchange_and_verify(code, login_state, cfg),
         :ok <- check_nonce(claims, login_state["nonce"]) do
      if mode == "bootstrap" do
        bootstrap_callback(conn, claims)
      else
        normal_callback(conn, claims, refresh_token)
      end
    else
      {:error, reason} ->
        Logger.warning("admin callback failed: #{inspect(reason)}")

        conn
        |> Phoenix.Controller.redirect(to: "/admin/login?error=auth_failed")
        |> halt()
    end
  end

  # Exchanges the code and verifies the ID token. Returns `{:ok, claims, refresh_token}`
  # where `refresh_token` is the OIDC RT (or nil when the provider granted none). A test
  # seam (`:admin_oidc_token_override`, a 0-arity fun) short-circuits the HTTP+JWT-verify
  # leg only — every surrounding check (state, nonce, mode branch) still runs. Mirrors the
  # existing `:oidc_metadata_override` seam. The seam may return either the legacy
  # `{:ok, claims}` (no RT) or the extended `{:ok, claims, refresh_token}` 3-tuple.
  defp exchange_and_verify(code, login_state, cfg) do
    case Application.get_env(:nebu_http, :admin_oidc_token_override) do
      fun when is_function(fun, 0) ->
        normalize_token_result(fun.())

      _ ->
        with {:ok, token_endpoint} <- discover(cfg.issuer, "token_endpoint"),
             {:ok, id_token, refresh_token} <-
               exchange_code(token_endpoint, code, login_state["verifier"], cfg),
             {:ok, claims} <- verify_id_token(id_token, login_state["mode"], cfg) do
          {:ok, claims, refresh_token}
        end
    end
  end

  # Verify the operator ID token. NORMAL mode uses the global caches (post-bootstrap they
  # ARE warm: issuer from OidcConfig, keys from JwksCache); only the aud is overridden to
  # the single client_id. Every other check (signature/alg/iss/exp/sub) is identical to
  # the Matrix bearer path.
  defp verify_id_token(id_token, "bootstrap", cfg) do
    # oidc-bootstrap-only-e2e-regressions (AC1/AC2): mid-bootstrap the global
    # JwksCache/OidcConfig are EMPTY (config still lives in bootstrap_draft). Fetch the
    # signing keys LOCALLY from the draft's JWKS URI (or discover from the draft issuer)
    # using the SAME TLS-verifying fetcher JwksCache uses, and verify with the draft
    # issuer + keys passed as overrides — WITHOUT warming the global caches (the Matrix
    # API must stay fail-closed until bootstrap completes). A fetch failure is a clean
    # tagged error so the callback logs + bounces rather than crashing the request.
    case Nebu.Web.JwksCache.fetch_keys_for(cfg.jwks_uri, cfg.issuer) do
      {:ok, keys} ->
        Nebu.Web.Plugs.OidcPlug.verify_token(id_token,
          issuer: cfg.issuer,
          audience: cfg.client_id,
          jwks: keys
        )

      :error ->
        {:error, :bootstrap_jwks_unavailable}
    end
  end

  defp verify_id_token(id_token, _mode, cfg) do
    Nebu.Web.Plugs.OidcPlug.verify_token(id_token, audience: cfg.client_id)
  end

  # Accept both the legacy 2-tuple and the extended 3-tuple from the override seam.
  defp normalize_token_result({:ok, claims}), do: {:ok, claims, nil}
  defp normalize_token_result({:ok, claims, refresh_token}), do: {:ok, claims, refresh_token}
  defp normalize_token_result({:error, _} = err), do: err

  # Normal admin login: enforce the admin-group gate, mint the session, land on the
  # dashboard (consistent with the bootstrap-completion landing; the AC "reaches
  # dashboard" expects this). The sidebar lets the operator reach rooms/users from there.
  defp normal_callback(conn, claims, refresh_token) do
    case check_admin(claims) do
      :ok ->
        provision_matrix_identity(claims)

        conn
        |> put_current_user(claims)
        |> store_refresh_token(refresh_token)
        |> Phoenix.Controller.redirect(to: "/admin/dashboard")
        |> halt()

      {:error, :not_admin} ->
        Logger.warning("admin callback denied: admin group claim absent")

        conn
        |> put_resp_content_type("text/plain")
        |> send_resp(403, "Access denied: admin group claim not present in token.")
        |> halt()
    end
  end

  # Bootstrap-mode callback (Go parity: CallbackHandler sc.Mode == "bootstrap"). The ID
  # token is verified but the admin-group gate is SKIPPED — no admin exists yet. The
  # authenticated sub/email are stashed in the draft (consumed by bootstrap_confirm_claim/2)
  # and the discovered claims are rendered as a selectable list. AC5: refuse if bootstrap
  # is already complete (defence-in-depth; login_start also refuses).
  defp bootstrap_callback(conn, claims) do
    cond do
      bootstrap_completed?() ->
        conn
        |> Phoenix.Controller.redirect(to: "/admin/login")
        |> halt()

      not is_binary(claims["sub"]) or claims["sub"] == "" ->
        conn
        |> put_resp_content_type("text/plain")
        |> send_resp(400, "invalid token: missing sub claim")
        |> halt()

      true ->
        put_draft("bootstrap_sub", claims["sub"])
        put_draft("bootstrap_email", claims["email"] || "")
        # SEC (Kassandra C1, claim-value injection): stash the verified token's discovered
        # claim VALUES server-side so bootstrap_confirm_claim/2 can reject any POSTed
        # admin_group_claim that is NOT one of them. This is exactly the set rendered on the
        # select-claim page (extract_discovered_claims/1) — the operator may only pick a
        # value that actually appeared in the token they authenticated with, so the org-wide
        # admin gate can never be decoupled from that token by a forged/free-form POST body.
        put_draft("bootstrap_claims", encode_discovered_claims(claims))
        # fix-bootstrap-admin-session-identity AC2: also stash the FULL verified claims map
        # (not the flattened bootstrap_claims list above, which dot-paths nested objects for
        # the claim-picker UI and is NOT usable as input to Nebu.Matrix.UserId.from_claims/2,
        # which does direct flat-key lookups like claims["preferred_username"]). This is what
        # lets bootstrap_confirm_claim/2 mint the session via the SAME put_current_user/2 path
        # normal_callback/2 uses, so matrix_user_id is derived identically to a subsequent
        # normal re-login of the same person. Draft storage is already server-side (no new
        # attack surface — same trust boundary as bootstrap_claims above).
        put_draft("bootstrap_full_claims", Jason.encode!(claims))

        conn
        |> Phoenix.Controller.redirect(to: "/admin/bootstrap/select-claim")
        |> halt()
    end
  end

  # Serialize the discovered {key, value} pairs as a JSON list of [key, value] lists
  # (tuples are not JSON-encodable). Decoded back into a value-set by confirm.
  defp encode_discovered_claims(claims) do
    claims
    |> extract_discovered_claims()
    |> Enum.map(fn {k, v} -> [k, v] end)
    |> Jason.encode!()
